segments.text: Man after the fall of Adam hath free-will as well to doe that which is good, as that which is euill, although it be in a diuers manner, that is, he hath free-wil to do• euill simplie, and without any externall aide: but to doe well, none at all, but by the grace of God preuenting, or guiding vs: the which grace notwithstanding euery man hath, and to the which grace it is in our free-will either to consent and togither worke with the same, or not. And therfore the power of free-will to doe that which is good & acceptable to God, is onely attenuated & weakened before conuersion, and therefore man can of himselfe worke a preparation to iustification.
